comments.text:
If you possess solid financial management skills, the need for insurance or social security becomes minimal, aside from covering health-related and emergency contingencies. Typically, accessing funds from these policies when needed is often cumbersome due to lengthy processing or strict withdrawal conditions. Furthermore, insurance companies allocate your premiums into investments such as bonds, equities, and other financial instruments, essentially capitalizing on your contributions to generate returns. For financially literate individuals, directly investing in these asset classes may provide greater liquidity and higher returns without relying on intermediaries like insurance providers.

These investments are also affected by currency devaluation, and inflation eats away the value of your currency. So by the time you retire, the millions you’ve saved would have significantly lost their purchasing power. If I were you, I’d invest not in insurance but in assets that appreciate in value, like gold, silver, and the US stock markets
